6260: Integrated help for operation, diagnostics, analysis and the MEMS database.
6262: Actuator tests can operate the pump, fan, valves, injector or ignition. Secure the vehicle, work in a ventilated area and run a command only when you understand its consequences.
6263: This help follows the active software language and remains scrollable and resizable on smaller screens.
6400: Connect the diagnostic interface, switch the ignition on, then select the serial port that is actually present in Options. Press Connect to open the ECU session. The communication indicators show link activity. Use Disconnect before intentionally removing the cable.
6401: The Overview tab groups the essential live engine information: engine speed, manifold pressure, temperatures, battery voltage, throttle, lambda, idle and ignition. Gauges and traces adapt to the window size so the same visual organization is preserved across display resolutions.
6402: The Settings tab contains the service corrections available for the ECU. Help bubbles explain each adjustment. The hot-idle correction used to decode 7D14-15 comes from the value actually configured in the software; it must not be hard-coded as a constant.
6403: The Errors tab displays faults and states reported by the ECU. Read and interpret the information before clearing anything. A new DTC can trigger the alert provided by the software. Do not clear a fault before recording its context.
6404: This tab can command supported actuators when the protocol state allows it. Fuel pump, fan, purge, lambda heater, IAC and other outputs must be tested with the vehicle secured. Never operate injector or ignition where this could cause starting, over-fuelling or electric shock.
6405: The All measurements tab presents parameters in a concise view with Parameter, Help bubble and Value. The displayed value uses the same decoding as the rest of the program. Fields that are not yet documented remain visible without inventing a conversion.
6406: This view exposes detailed MEMS data and decoded values. It is useful for comparing an interpreted measurement with the bytes or fields received from the ECU and for retaining access to advanced technical information.
6407: The ECU / ROSCO tab lets you observe session exchanges and documented commands, including D0, D1, D2, F0 and session changes F2 to F5. TX and RX are shown in hexadecimal. D3 recoding remains intentionally blocked until its write procedure is sufficiently established.
6408: Automatic diagnostics checks received values and classifies them as normal, warnings or anomalies. It can capture a reference, compare measurements and export a report. Primary coil charge time is monitored around the 1.9–3.1 ms range when battery voltage is close to 14 V.
6409: The Analysis tab loads compatible CSV and TXT logs, lets you choose channels to display and overlays curves to compare their evolution. Use the navigation and scale tools to inspect a precise area of the recording.
6410: The capture button saves an image of the program window. The integrated viewer lets you browse captures, open them enlarged and delete them after confirmation. Images can be zoomed and scrolled when they are larger than the window.
6411: The integrated database groups technical references for MEMS 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9: commands, data, DTCs, wiring, connectors, sheets and resources. Diagrams remain associated with their corresponding data and user-facing text is displayed in the active language.
6412: Global search indexes database tables, XML sheets and registered resources. You can search for a code, command, sensor, value, connector or technical term. Short queries such as IAT, D0 or P0115 are ranked according to their technical category.
6413: Options lets you select the COM port, units, theme, language and available preferences. The COM port list must reflect serial ports actually present in Windows. Supported languages are French, English, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and German.
6414: The interface keeps the same structure in light or dark theme and remains proportional to the available space. Pages that are too tall use scrolling and the tab bar keeps pages accessible on smaller displays.
6415: Three-dot help bubbles provide a short explanation directly beside the relevant parameter. Use them before a command or adjustment whose effect is not obvious. They also follow the active language.
6416: The project targets Rover MEMS 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9 families. Functions actually available depend on the ECU, vehicle and session state. For MEMS 1.9, the physical link uses K-Line but the application protocol remains proprietary MEMS/ROSCO; it is not generic OBD-II diagnostics.
6417: No communication: check ignition, COM port, cable, ECU power and grounds. Abnormal MAP value: check vacuum and hoses. Unstable idle: check idle switch, IAC, air leaks, engine temperature and corrections. Lambda fault: check heater, wiring and sensor activity. Coil charge outside range: check battery voltage, primary circuit, coil and harness.
